name: E-commerce
one_liner: Online sale of goods through first-party retailers and third-party marketplaces, where economics are defined by customer acquisition cost, fulfillment cost per order, and repeat purchasing.
how_it_makes_money: First-party sellers earn product margin like any retailer, while marketplaces take a commission (take rate) on third-party sales and charge for fulfillment and advertising. Mature platforms increasingly rely on high-margin advertising and subscription fees to subsidize low-margin product sales and fast delivery.
revenue_formula: Revenue = site visitors × conversion rate × average order value
Marketplace revenue = GMV × take rate (commissions + fulfillment + ads)
Customer value = orders per year × AOV × contribution margin × expected lifetime
cost_structure: Cost of goods (for first-party): the product itself
Fulfillment: picking, packing, and warehouse labor
Shipping and last-mile: often the most scrutinized cost per order
Customer acquisition and performance marketing: paid search and social ads
Returns: reverse logistics and write-offs, especially heavy in apparel
margins: Most pure-play e-commerce operators run low or negative operating margins, while scaled marketplaces earn healthier profits because advertising and seller services carry high margins. The spread depends on order density, return rates, AOV relative to shipping cost, and reliance on paid acquisition.

key_metrics.name: Gross merchandise value (GMV)
key_metrics.what: Total value of goods sold on the platform, the headline scale metric for marketplaces.

key_metrics.name: Take rate
key_metrics.what: Share of GMV the platform keeps as revenue, reflecting pricing power over sellers.

key_metrics.name: Conversion rate
key_metrics.what: Share of site visits that result in an order, a direct lever on revenue.

key_metrics.name: Average order value (AOV)
key_metrics.what: Spend per order, which determines whether shipping costs can be covered.

key_metrics.name: CAC and LTV
key_metrics.what: Cost to acquire a customer versus lifetime profit, the core test of unit economics.

key_metrics.name: Contribution margin per order
key_metrics.what: Profit per order after product, fulfillment, shipping, and payment costs.

key_metrics.name: Return rate
key_metrics.what: Share of orders sent back, a major profit drain in apparel and footwear.

trends: Low-price cross-border marketplaces such as Temu and Shein reshaping competition, with tariff and de minimis rule changes altering their model
Advertising becoming a major profit engine for large marketplaces
Faster delivery promises through regionalized fulfillment networks
Social and creator-led commerce through platforms like TikTok Shop
Rising customer acquisition costs pushing DTC brands back into wholesale and physical retail
AI shopping assistants and agentic checkout changing product discovery
